clues.title: Coverage: low-quality brownish camera, round blur
text: The vast majority of the coverage in India was taken with what’s commonly referred to as “shitcam”, which is a **low-quality camera** that can typically be recognised by the brownish colours and often, but not always, by a large circular blur covering the Street View car.
NOTE: Within Asia, Nepal is also entirely “shitcam”, while it’s also common in Cambodia and can rarely be seen in Sri Lanka and Bangladesh.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Most coverage uses a low-quality camera with brownish colours and often a big round blur over the car. Nepal is entirely like this; Cambodia often, Sri Lanka and Bangladesh rarely.

clues.title: Coverage: Gen 4 smallcam, low with big blur
text: All the Generation 4 coverage in India was taken using the smallcam, which is mounted lower than regular Generation 4 and has a relatively big circular blur with a small protrusion at the front. The blur can also be fully transparent, making it harder to spot.

images.caption: Four panels labelled front panned down, front panned straight, back panned down and good blur (front)

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Gen 4 coverage was filmed with the smallcam, mounted lower than normal, with a big round blur and a small bump at the front. The blur can be see-through and hard to spot.

clues.title: Coverage: many Gen 3 walkers among poor camera
text: While most of India is covered in shitcam, there is also a significant amount of **Generation 3 trekkers** throughout the country.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Most coverage is poor quality, but lots of Gen 3 walker (backpack) coverage is spread across the country.

images.caption: Sample of several Indian scripts side by side

clues.summary: Many scripts are used across the country, and most help you narrow down the region.

clues.title: Plate: long; white, yellow commercial, green EV
text: Indian licence plates are typically fairly long, with the most common design being white. Commercial vehicles typically use yellow plates, while electric vehicles use green.

images.caption: Indian plates: standard white, yellow commercial and green electric

clues.title: Sign: black-and-white striped signposts
text: India typically has **black and white striped signposts**.
NOTE: Bangladesh, Nepal and Sri Lanka also have black and white signposts.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Signposts are often striped black and white. Bangladesh, Nepal and Sri Lanka have them too.

clues.title: Pole: square concrete with trident top
text: The most common Indian utility pole is a concrete square pole with a trident pole top.
Beware that many regions have their own distinct poles and poletops.
NOTE: Indian poles will almost always be made of concrete or metal. Wooden poles are extremely uncommon.

images.caption: A red circle zooms in on the metal hardware at the top of the concrete pole

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: The most common pole is square concrete with a trident top. Many regions have their own pole types. Poles are almost always concrete or metal; wood is extremely rare.

clues.title: Language: Devanagari script, line on top of words
text: **Hindi** is the most common language in India and can be found in many central and northern regions. It uses the [Devanagari script](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devanagari), which can be recognised by the line going through the top of each word and the straight vertical lines found in the majority of all letters.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Hindi is the most common language, in central and northern areas. Its Devanagari script has a line along the top of each word and many straight vertical strokes.

clues.title: Language: Devanagari with the letter ळ
text: **Marathi**, found in Maharashtra, also uses the Devanagari script, however it sometimes uses the letter **ळ** which is not found in Hindi.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: In the west (Maharashtra), the language also uses Devanagari, but sometimes has the letter ळ, which Hindi lacks.

clues.title: Language: softer script, broken top line, ਨ ਲ ਅ
text: **Punjabi** can be found in Punjab in northwestern India. While the script looks somewhat similar to Hindi, it can generally be differentiated by the softer shape of the letters and the horizontal bar being broken over certain letters. It also has some distinctly different features, such as the letters **ਨ**, **ਲ** and** ਅ **as well as a [diacritic](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/%E0%A9%81) in the shape of a soft curve beneath a letter.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: In the north-west (Punjab), the script resembles Hindi but is softer, with a top bar broken over some letters. Look for ਨ, ਲ, ਅ and a soft curved mark under a letter.

clues.title: Language: Devanagari-like script without top line
text: **Gujarati**, found in Gujarat, has a script with several similarities to the Hindi script, however it notably lacks the horizontal line at the top of every word.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: In the west (Gujarat), the script is similar to Hindi but has no horizontal line along the top of words.

clues.title: Language: Bengali script, left-facing triangles
text: **Bengali** is found in northeastern India and has a similar look to Devanagari (Hindi), however it can usually be recognised by the many letters featuring left-facing triangular shapes.
NOTE: This is also the language found in Bangladesh.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: In the north-east, the script is like Devanagari but with many letters featuring left-facing triangles. Bangladesh uses the same language.

clues.title: Language: Bengali script plus ৰ and ৱ
text: **Assamese**, mainly found in Assam, also uses the Bengali script, with the addition of some characters, most notably **ৰ** and **ৱ**.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: In the north-east (Assam), the Bengali script is used with extra characters, notably ৰ and ৱ.

clues.title: Language: round curvy script, squiggly tails
text: **Kannada** is found in Karnataka and has a script with a lot of smooth curves and small circles. It is very similar to the Telugu script, with Telugu having one additional feature described in the next tip. Many characters also feature a distinct squiggly tail in the top right corner, which is less common in Telugu.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: In the south (Karnataka), the script has smooth curves and small circles, close to Telugu. Many letters have a squiggly tail in the top right, less common in Telugu.

clues.title: Language: Kannada-like script with checkmark marks on top
text: **Telugu**, found in Telangana and Andhra Pradesh, has a script very similar to Kannada, but you’ll often see diacritics resembling checkmarks at the top of letters.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: In the south-east (Telangana, Andhra Pradesh), the script is very similar to Kannada but often has checkmark-like marks on top of letters.

clues.title: Language: curves, straight lines and 90-degree angles
text: The **Tamil** script is found in Tamil Nadu and has a distinct combination of curves, straight lines and **90° angles**. Some letters also have diacritics shaped like dots.
NOTE: Tamil is also commonly found in Sri Lanka.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: In the far south (Tamil Nadu), the script mixes curves, straight lines and right angles, and some letters have dot marks. Tamil is also common in Sri Lanka.

clues.title: Language: curvy script with wide arches, skull-like
text: The **Oriya** script is found in Odisha and has a curvy look, with many letters having wide semi-circles covering the top. Many letters have a distinct diacritic in the shape of a wide curve above the top of the letter. A useful mnemonic is that the shape of the characters resembles a [skull emoji](/images/india/skullemoji.png?).

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: In the east (Odisha), the script is curvy with wide semi-circles on top of many letters and a wide curve mark above others. Letters look like a skull emoji.

clues.title: Language: simple curvy letters with upside-down U shapes
text: The **Malayalam** script can be found in Kerala and mostly consists of somewhat simple-looking curvy letters, often containing upside-down **U-shapes**.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: In the south-west (Kerala), the script is mostly simple, curvy letters, often with upside-down U shapes.

clues.title: Language: Meitei script, vertical lines and right angles
text: **Manipuri**, also called Meitei, is the official language of Manipur. It is written using the Meitei script, which can be recognised by its many vertical lines and right angles.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: In the north-east (Manipur), Meitei script has many vertical lines and right angles.

clues.title: Language: Latin-script Mizo
text: **Mizo**, found in Mizoram,** **is the language most commonly found on the Indian coverage other than English, which uses the **Latin script**.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: In the north-east (Mizoram), the main language other than English is Mizo, written in the Latin alphabet.

clues.title: Language: almost only English, north-east hills
text: While **English** can be found anywhere in India, Meghalaya is the only region which almost exclusively uses English.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: English appears everywhere, but one north-east state (Meghalaya) uses it almost exclusively.

clues.title: Vehicles: yellow tuk tuks with black roofs
text: **Yellow tuk tuks** with **black roofs** are common in the southern Indian states of Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, and Tamil Nadu.
NOTE: They can also rarely be found [elsewhere](https://www.google.com/maps/@26.0016426,92.846562,3a,36.4y,218.5h,82.82t/data=!3m6!1e1!3m4!1sNm7a6dUzWhFoZT4TDVehnQ!2e0!7i13312!8i6656?entry=ttu).

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Yellow auto rickshaws with black roofs are common in the south and south-east states (Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu). They rarely appear elsewhere.

clues.title: Pole: concrete poles with holes
text: **Concrete holey poles** are unique to Gujarat and the Union territory of Daman and Diu, and Dadra and Nagar Haveli.
Gujarat uses a variety of poletops, some of which can be used to identify other states. Beware that holey poles generally take precedence over poletop metas.
NOTE: They are rarely found in other states especially Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh, and Chhattisgarh.

images.caption: A red circle zooms in on the holes in the concrete pole
A red circle zooms in on the holes in the concrete pole

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Concrete poles with holes are unique to the west coast state (Gujarat) and two nearby union territories. Rare in neighbouring states. Holey poles take priority over other pole clues.

clues.title: Pole: poles split in two sections, like Brazil's
text: Poles divided in** two sections**, in a similar fashion to [Brazilian poles](https://www.google.com/maps/@-24.9571111,-53.4509436,3a,51.7y,197.35h,89.21t/data=!3m6!1e1!3m4!1s5lhJHp3bn7bMpsWZg81SCA!2e0!7i16384!8i8192?entry=ttu), are common in Andhra Pradesh and Telangana.

images.caption: A red circle zooms in on the pole split into two sections
A red circle zooms in on the pole split into two sections

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Poles divided in two sections, like Brazilian ones, are common in the south-east (Andhra Pradesh, Telangana).

differs.how: Brazilian poles look alike but have other differences

clues.title: Pole: metal poles with mesh pattern
text: Metal poles with a **mesh pattern** are commonly found in Sikkim.

images.caption: A red circle zooms in on the metal pole's mesh pattern

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Metal poles with a mesh pattern are common in the Himalayan north-east (Sikkim).

clues.title: Pole: metal poles with holes
text: **Metal holey poles** are common in Kerala.

images.caption: A red circle zooms in on the holes in the metal pole

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Metal poles with holes are common in the south-west (Kerala).

clues.title: Pole: thin grey metal poles, often two together
text: Thin **grey metal poles** are seen all over northeastern India and in the Himalayan region of [Uttarakhand](https://www.google.com/maps/@31.0147909,78.8786745,3a,62.8y,249.59h,99.19t/data=!3m6!1e1!3m4!1sSGL6A0GbRH6cTLDnW-EABw!2e0!7i13312!8i6656?entry=ttu) and Himachal Pradesh. You will commonly see two of these poles in close proximity.

images.caption: Two thin grey metal poles stand side by side

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Thin grey metal poles, often two next to each other, are common across the north-east and the Himalayan north (Uttarakhand, Himachal Pradesh).

clues.title: Electricity meter: mint green with small window squares
text: Electricity counters in Punjab are usually **mint green** with small **window-like squares**. They can rarely be seen in Haryana.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: In the north-west (Punjab), electricity meters are usually mint green with small window-like squares. Rarely seen in Haryana.

clues.title: Pole: small window-shaped metal pole tops
text: Small metal poletops in the shape of a **window** are found in Punjab and Haryana.

images.caption: A red circle zooms in on the small window-shaped metal top of the pole
Close-up of a small window-shaped metal pole top

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Small window-shaped metal pole tops are found in the north-west (Punjab, Haryana).

clues.title: Pole: concrete trident, middle insulator on top
text: In Karnataka, and sometimes in Haryana, you can find **trident poletops** on **concrete poles** where the central insulator is attached directly to the top of the pole, while the other two are attached to a horizontal crossbar positioned slightly further down. There is also a [variant](https://www.google.com/maps/@12.2009963,75.8093964,3a,15y,235.71h,103.89t/data=!3m6!1e1!3m4!1sbTl5fPNbWHR5rkj6eAuIPw!2e0!7i13312!8i6656?entry=ttu) having several bars instead of one.

images.caption: A red circle zooms in on the concrete trident top with a middle insulator on top

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: On concrete poles in the south-west (Karnataka) and sometimes Haryana, the middle insulator sits on top and the other two on a crossbar slightly lower. A variant has several bars.

clues.title: Pole: trident top on all-metal poles
text: In Manipur you can often find **trident poletops **on poles made entirely out of **metal**. They sometimes have small bars on the top of the trident.

images.caption: A red circle zooms in on the trident top of the all-metal pole
A red circle zooms in on the trident top of the all-metal pole

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: In the far north-east (Manipur), trident tops sit on all-metal poles, sometimes with small bars on top of the trident.

clues.title: Pole: upside-down triangle top below the pole top
text: **Upside down triangle poletops** placed below the top of the pole are commonly found in Maharashtra, Chhattisgarh, and less commonly in Madhya Pradesh.

images.caption: A red circle zooms in on the upside-down triangle below the pole top

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Upside-down triangle pole tops, placed below the top of the pole, are common in the west and centre (Maharashtra, Chhattisgarh) and less often Madhya Pradesh.

clues.title: Pole: upside-down A bar below pole top
text: Poles in Madhya Pradesh often have a metal bar shaped like an **upside down A** slightly below the top of the pole.

images.caption: A red circle zooms in on the upside-down A-shaped bar below the pole top
A red circle zooms in on the upside-down A-shaped bar below the pole top

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: In the centre (Madhya Pradesh), poles often have an upside-down A-shaped metal bar slightly below the top.

clues.title: Pole: upside-down trapezoid connector
text: A connector on the pole which looks like an upside down [trapezoid](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/6/67/Trapezoid_2_%28PSF%29.png) is most common in Chhattisgarh and somewhat common in Meghalaya, Tripura and Maharashtra, but can rarely be found in many other states.
NOTE: They can also be paired with Holey Poles in Gujarat and Ladder Poles in Andhra Pradesh, thus only use the trapezoid when no other pole meta is present.

images.caption: A red circle zooms in on the upside-down trapezoid connector below the crossbar
A red circle zooms in on the upside-down trapezoid connector below the crossbar

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: An upside-down trapezoid connector is most common in the centre-east (Chhattisgarh), fairly common in a few north-east states and the west, and rare elsewhere. Use it only if no other pole clue shows.

clues.title: Pole: tall narrow rectangle pole top
text: A variety of poletops attached to the pole with two vertical bars forming a **tall and narrow rectangle** can be found in West Bengal.

images.caption: Two pole tops side by side; the right one has a tall narrow rectangle on top

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Pole tops attached with two vertical bars forming a tall, narrow rectangle are found in the east (West Bengal).

clues.title: Pole: two crossbars with side supports, diagonal braces
text: In West Bengal you may also find poletops containing two crossbars which are connected to each other** **with thin vertical supports on either side. The lower bar is connected on either side to the pole with diagonal supports.

images.caption: A red circle zooms in on two crossbars with side supports and diagonal bars

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: In the east (West Bengal), pole tops with two crossbars joined by thin vertical supports on each side, with the lower bar braced by diagonals to the pole.

clues.title: Pole: mix of even and uneven top
text: In the northeast you may find poles with a combination of an **even and uneven** poletop.

images.caption: Two pole tops, one with an even crossbar and one with an uneven one

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: In the north-east you may find poles combining an even and an uneven top.

clues.title: Pole: two diagonal bars forming a < shape
text: Poles with two diagonal bars forming a ‘<’ shape are common in Meghalaya and Arunachal Pradesh and occasionally found in Assam.

images.caption: A red circle zooms in on two diagonal bars forming a < shape

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Poles with two diagonal bars in a < shape are common in two north-east states (Meghalaya, Arunachal Pradesh) and occasionally Assam.

clues.title: Pole: two crossbars, each with two insulators
text: In Assam, Meghalaya and Mizoram you commonly see poles with **two crossbars**, each with two insulators. If there are [more than two bars](https://maps.app.goo.gl/eC7DQnwG2P1YPs9Y7), you should be in Meghalaya or Mizoram.
NOTE: They can rarely be seen in other states.

images.caption: A red circle zooms in on two crossbars, each with two insulators

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: In the north-east (Assam, Meghalaya, Mizoram), poles often have two crossbars with two insulators each. More than two bars means Meghalaya or Mizoram. Rare elsewhere.

clues.title: Pole: trident with middle tip bent 90 degrees
text: Trident poletops with the tip of the middle bar bent at a 90° angle can be found in Assam.

images.caption: A red circle zooms in on the trident with its middle tip bent 90 degrees
A red circle zooms in on the trident with its middle tip bent 90 degrees

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Trident pole tops with the middle tip bent at a right angle are found in the north-east (Assam).

clues.title: Pole: short crossbar above longer crossbar
text: Poletops with a short crossbar above a longer crossbar can be found in Goa.

images.caption: A red circle zooms in on a short crossbar above a longer crossbar

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Pole tops with a short crossbar above a longer one are found on the west coast (Goa).

clues.title: Pole: one black stripe between two white
text: Markings on poles and trees, consisting of one black stripe in-between two white ones, are common in Tamil Nadu.

images.caption: A tree and a pole painted with one black stripe between two white ones

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Markings on poles and trees of one black stripe between two white ones are common in the far south (Tamil Nadu).

clues.title: Pole paint: five or more thin black-yellow stripes
text: Pole paint consisting of five or more thin black and yellow stripes can be found in Delhi.

images.caption: A pole painted with thin black and yellow stripes

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Pole paint of five or more thin black and yellow stripes is found in the capital region (Delhi).

clues.title: Pole paint: exactly four thick black-yellow stripes
text: Pole paint consisting of exactly four thicker black and yellow stripes can be found in Bihar.

images.caption: Poles painted with four thick black-yellow stripes
Close-up of poles painted with four thick black-yellow stripes

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Pole paint of exactly four thicker black and yellow stripes is found in the north-east plains (Bihar).

clues.title: Plants: tree trunks with four red-white stripes
text: In Bihar, and less commonly Jharkhand, you may find trees with **four red and white stripes** painted near the bottom.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Trees with four red and white stripes near the bottom are found in the north-east plains (Bihar) and less commonly Jharkhand.

clues.title: Pole: small yellow markings
text: Small **yellow pole markings** are commonly found in Kerala.
NOTE: Similar stickers can rarely be found in other states.

images.caption: A red circle zooms in on a small yellow marking with letters and numbers on the pole

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Small yellow pole markings are common in the south-west (Kerala). Similar stickers rarely appear in other states.

clues.title: Houses: rounded roof tiles, messy rows
text: **Rounded roof tiles** are common in central India. They often appear disorganised and are kept in rows/columns that are not completely straight.

images.caption: Mud house with a rounded-tile roof; the red circle magnifies the tiles

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Rounded roof tiles are common in central India, often laid untidily in not quite straight rows and columns.

clues.title: Houses: bright orange flat tiles with middle ridge
text: Roofs in southern India are characterised by more organised tiles that are bright orange and flat with a ridge in the middle. It is particularly common in Tamil Nadu.
NOTE: Similarly shaped tiles with a darker brown colour are common further north.

images.caption: Orange flat roof tiles with a middle ridge; the red circle magnifies the tiles

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: In the south, roofs have tidy, bright orange flat tiles with a ridge in the middle, especially in the far south. Similar darker brown tiles are common further north.

clues.title: Houses: flat tiles with small diamond bump
text: Flat roof tiles, similar to the ones found in the south, with a small **diamond shaped protrusion** in the middle, are commonly found in and around West Bengal.

images.caption: Flat roof tiles with a small diamond bump; the red circle magnifies the tiles

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Flat roof tiles like those in the south, but with a small diamond-shaped bump in the middle, are common in and around the east (West Bengal).

clues.title: Houses: large hip roofs of corrugated metal
text: Large [hip roofs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hip_roof) made of corrugated sheet metal are found in West Bengal and adjacent areas in Bihar and Odisha.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Large hip roofs of corrugated sheet metal are found in the east (West Bengal) and nearby parts of Bihar and Odisha.

clues.title: Houses: metal roofs with small triangle near the top
text: Metal roofs, with a small triangle near the top, are common in Northeast India.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Metal roofs with a small triangle near the top are common in the north-east.

clues.title: Houses: square panels separated by thin beams
text: Houses made of **square panels** separated by thin beams are found in Northeast India.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Houses made of square panels divided by thin beams are found in the north-east.

clues.title: Houses: thatched roofs, hay mounds in the east
text: Houses or huts with **thatched roofs** are mainly found along the east coast and northern plains. Large [hay mounds](https://goo.gl/maps/kzVojHKUKbsSn9hN7) are also generally more common in this region. Note that thatched roofs from Uttar Pradesh to Odisha tend to be made of [fine pieces of hay](https://goo.gl/maps/kzVojHKUKbsSn9hN7) whereas thatched roofs from Odisha to Tamil Nadu tend to be made of dried [palm fans](https://goo.gl/maps/JQrA1smY5vWAYjee9).

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Thatched houses or huts are mainly along the east coast and northern plains, with large hay mounds. From the north to the east they use fine hay; from the east to the far south, dried palm fans.

clues.title: Buildings: white-domed temples with Khanda symbol
text: [Gurdwaras](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gurdwara), which can typically be recognised by their white domes and ornate walls, are most common in Punjab. You can also sometimes recognise them by the [Sikh Khanda symbol](https://maps.app.goo.gl/aKK5UzU4N2Qks3kT9), which represents the religion.

images.caption: A white-domed temple; the circle at bottom left shows the Khanda symbol

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Gurdwaras, Sikh temples, have white domes and ornate walls, and often the Khanda symbol. Most common in the north-west (Punjab).

clues.title: Houses: wealthy modern homes in two developed states
text: Goa and Kerala are two of the most developed states in India and often have very **wealthy and modern homes**.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Two of the most developed states (Goa, Kerala) often have very wealthy, modern homes.

clues.title: Plants: chir pines, smooth cone crowns, very long needles
text: [Chir pines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pinus_roxburghii) are more or less exclusive to Uttarakhand, Himachal Pradesh, Jammu and Kashmir as well as in westernmost Arunachal Pradesh. These pines can be identified from their generally smooth-looking conical or spherical crowns with very long needles.

images.caption: Chir pines with smooth cone-shaped crowns; the circle zooms in on the very long needles

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Chir pines grow almost only in the Himalayan north and the far west of the north-east. They have smooth conical or round crowns and very long needles.

clues.title: Plants: Khasi pines, jagged crowns
text: [Khasi pines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pinus_kesiya) are mainly found in Meghalaya and Manipur. While the needles appear similar to those of chir pines, the overall crown formed by its branches will appear more jagged and disorganised.

images.caption: Khasi pines with jagged crowns; the circle zooms in on the foliage

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Khasi pines are mainly in two north-east states (Meghalaya, Manipur). Needles look like chir pine but the crown is more jagged and messy.

clues.title: Plants: spiny cactus-like fences
text: This type of cacti ([Euphorbia neriifolia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euphorbia_neriifolia)) can commonly be seen as part of fences throughout Gujarat, western Maharashtra and the southern half of Rajasthan.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: This spurge (Euphorbia neriifolia) is common in fences across the west (Gujarat, western Maharashtra, southern Rajasthan).

clues.title: Plants: lollipop-shaped palms
text: Palmyra Palms have a **round crown** with** fan shaped leaves** and a trunk with consistent thickness, giving them a lollipop shape. If you see them in large numbers you should be in the south or east of the country.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Palmyra palms have a round crown of fan leaves on a trunk of even thickness, like a lollipop. Many of them mean the south or east.

clues.title: Plants: very thin palm trunk with small crown
text: Areca Palms can be recognised by their **very thin trunk** and a small crown. They are mainly found near the southwestern coast, in the northeast and on the Andaman and Nicobar Islands.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Areca palms have very thin trunks and small crowns. Mostly on the south-west coast, the north-east and the Andaman and Nicobar islands.

clues.title: Plants: date palms in dry central regions
text: **Date palms** are commonly found in drier areas of the central regions of India where there are fewer tropical and coastal palms.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Date palms are common in drier central areas, where there are fewer tropical and coastal palms.

clues.title: Crops: oil palm plantations in the south-east
text: **Oil palm **plantations are most commonly found in the panhandle of Andhra Pradesh, especially near the eastern border with Telangana.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Oil palm plantations are most common in the eastern panhandle of Andhra Pradesh, especially near the Telangana border.

clues.title: Crops: tea plantations in north-east and far south
text: **Tea plantations** can be found in the northeast and the far south.
NOTE: If you find tea plantations in a [flat area](https://goo.gl/maps/gS9CcgaZc9GzH6186), you are likely in Assam or northeastern West Bengal, near the Assam border.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Tea plantations are found in the north-east and the far south. Tea on flat ground means Assam or north-east West Bengal.

clues.title: Crops: sugarcane in the north and south-west
text: **Sugarcane** is most commonly found in the north in and around Uttar Pradesh, and in the southwest.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Sugarcane is most common in the north, around Uttar Pradesh, and in the south-west.

clues.title: Crops: cotton in the west
text: **Cotton** is commonly found in the western parts of India, particularly in Gujarat and Maharashtra.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Cotton is common in western India, especially Gujarat and Maharashtra.

clues.title: Crops: canola in the north-west

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Canola is mostly found in and around Rajasthan.

clues.summary: The tallest mountains by far are in the Himalayas.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: In Ladakh and northern Himachal Pradesh, the Himalayas are extremely dry with almost no plants.

clues.summary: The northern plains, the Ganges valley, are very fertile with extremely flat, open fields.

clues.summary: Distinctly dark soil is mainly found in the west (Maharashtra) and adjacent regions.

clues.title: Landscape: red soil in several regions
text: **Red soil** can be found in several regions, but mainly near the southern west coast and in and around Chhattisgarh and western Odisha.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Red soil is found near the southern west coast and around Chhattisgarh and western Odisha.

clues.title: Landscape: dry sandy western desert

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: The west of Rajasthan is dry with sandy soil.

clues.title: Landscape: plateau-topped ridges of the western mountains
text: The Western Ghats Mountains in the western part of Maharashtra can be recognised by their **distinct ridgelines**, often having plateaus rather than peaks. The northern part is drier while the southern part has more vegetation.

NOTE: During the [rainy season](https://www.google.com/maps/@19.5669899,73.7237394,3a,42y,336.38h,97.72t,359.97r/data=!3m6!1e1!3m4!1sfFjQwbXx-Aro9gPWDaPH5Q!2e0!7i13312!8i6656?entry=ttu) the mountains will turn green and appear quite different.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: The Western Ghats in western Maharashtra have distinct ridgelines, often plateaus not peaks. The north is drier, the south greener. In the rainy season they turn green.

clues.title: Landscape: lush valleys, eroded hills with small peaks
text: The landscape in Mizoram mainly consists of lush, green valleys with fairly low vegetation with eroded hillsides having many small peaks scattered around.

NOTE: A somewhat similar landscape can be found in [Meghalaya](https://www.google.com/maps/@25.3870998,91.7617742,3a,40.2y,128.95h,86.43t/data=!3m6!1e1!3m4!1s9EK2RjZ-ChZWuNyxjcwwvA!2e0!7i13312!8i6656?entry=ttu), however rather than distinct peaks, the hillsides will have a mostly smooth and flat top.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: In the far north-east (Mizoram), lush green valleys with low plants and eroded hillsides with many small peaks. Meghalaya is similar, but its hills have smooth flat tops instead of peaks.

clues.title: Vehicles: large square-shaped cars
text: Large visible, **square shaped cars** can be found in the areas shown on the map.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: In the north-east, fences made of thin wooden sticks in a square pattern are common.

clues.title: Signs: planned city, sector and numbered streets
text: The City of Chandigarh is a **planned industrial city**. As a result, the city features a lot of unique infrastructure, such as [blue signs](https://goo.gl/maps/HAYdSmx9sEsf2kbZ8) mentioning sectors and industrial areas, round yellow markings on street lights, and [street signs](https://www.google.com/maps/@30.7499192,76.7780503,3a,16.1y,130.5h,95.4t/data=!3m6!1e1!3m4!1sPVs101xGkIhtQvDG4dwKtA!2e0!7i13312!8i6656?entry=ttu) which will typically feature [several numbers](https://www.google.com/maps/@30.7250865,76.7767257,3a,15y,43.08h,74.38t/data=!3m6!1e1!3m4!1shEU9Ii83j_XOg74Ltm5G1Q!2e0!7i13312!8i6656?entry=ttu) rather than street names.

NOTE: The nearby cities of [Sahibzada Ajit Singh Nagar](https://www.google.com/maps/@30.7021706,76.7282816,3a,15y,307.52h,103.68t/data=!3m6!1e1!3m4!1sq0D20ET6KxQ-CQ2ZRgdqog!2e0!7i13312!8i6656?entry=ttu) and [Panchkula](https://www.google.com/maps/@30.6802307,76.8513495,3a,15y,85.06h,89.37t/data=!3m6!1e1!3m4!1sOcviMvOxgJKg32g23wdDhg!2e0!7i13312!8i6656?entry=ttu) are also planned industrial cities, which feature somewhat similar signs.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: A planned industrial city has blue signs naming sectors and industrial areas, round yellow marks on street lights, and street signs with several numbers instead of names. Two nearby planned cities have similar signs.

clues.title: Vehicles: orange and bright green buses
text: **Orange** and **bright green buses** are typically found in Delhi.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Orange and bright green buses are typical of the capital region.

clues.title: Roads: separated middle bus lanes
text: On large roads in Ahmedabad and Surat you can find separated middle lanes for buses. Beware that people will [still often drive](https://goo.gl/maps/HZ9K2MLEwhcoGZu89) in these lanes.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: On big roads in two western cities there are separated middle lanes for buses, though people often drive in them anyway.

clues.title: Vehicles: black taxis with yellow roofs
text: **Black Taxis** with **yellow roofs** are found in Meghalaya and [Mumbai](https://goo.gl/maps/tWXnBGQDKaQm9Z3D9).

clues.summary: Black taxis with yellow roofs appear in one north-east state and in the big west-coast city.

clues.summary: In the Himalayan north-east (Sikkim), taxis often have a painted yellow hood or a small yellow circle on it.

text: The area on the border of Telangana and Karnataka often have houses with roofs made out of distinctly thin grey bricks. clues.summary: Near the border of two southern states (Telangana, Karnataka), roofs often use thin grey bricks, and similar grey rocks appear in walls and scattered in stockyards.

text: **White painted clay huts** are found in northwestern Bihar and northeastern Uttar Pradesh.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: White-painted clay huts are found in the north-west of Bihar and north-east of Uttar Pradesh.

clues.title: Plants: tall Japanese cedars with narrow fluffy crowns
text: [Japanese cedar trees](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cryptomeria) can typically be recognised by their significant height combined with their narrow, fluffy-looking crowns. They are most commonly found near the border of Sikkim and West Bengal, as well as in Meghalaya.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Japanese cedars are very tall with narrow fluffy crowns. Most common near the border of Sikkim and West Bengal, and in Meghalaya.

clues.title: Plants: Himalayan cedar on mountain roads
text: The [Himalayan cedar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cedrus_deodara) is most commonly seen on the NH34 from Harsil to Gangotri, as well as around the city of [Shimla](https://goo.gl/maps/ddvgGQyNkwkpPggS9).

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Himalayan cedar is most common on NH34 from Harsil to Gangotri and around Shimla.

clues.title: Plants: pines with hanging downward needles
text: The [Bhutan white pine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pinus_bhutanica) can be recognised by its hanging needles all pointing downwards. They are mainly found in the Mechuka Valley as well as near the Bhutan border in Arunachal Pradesh.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: The Bhutan white pine has hanging, downward-pointing needles. It is mainly in a far north-east valley and near the Bhutan border in Arunachal Pradesh.

clues.title: Plants: doum palms with several branches
text: [Doum palms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hyphaene_thebaica), which appear similar to Palmyra palms but with **multiple branches**, are almost exclusive to the union territory of Diu.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Doum palms look like palmyra palms but with several branches. They are almost only on one small western union territory (Diu).

clues.title: Plants: carnivorous pitcher plants by the road
text: The endangered [Indian pitcher plant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepenthes_khasiana) is exclusive to the Khasi Hills, which are mainly in Meghalaya. They can occasionally be spotted on road sides, especially on the NH206 north of Umlārem.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: The endangered Indian pitcher plant lives only in the Khasi Hills (Meghalaya). You may spot it by the road, especially on NH206 north of one village.

clues.title: Landscape: barren brown hills on the Himalayan edge
text: The western half of Uttarakhand is typically **far** **more barren** than the other Himalayan regions, due to logging and erosion. The coverage northwest of Dehradun on the Himachal Pradesh Border has some especially barren hills full of brown grass and small roads next to cliffs.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: The west of Uttarakhand is much more barren than other Himalayan areas due to logging and erosion. North-west of Dehradun there are barren hills of brown grass and small roads next to cliffs.

clues.title: Landscape: snowy mountains, brown grass, hanging pines
text: The Mechuka valley is the only place in Northeast India where snowy mountains are visible. The valley contains brownish grass and a plethora of Bhutan white pine. [North of Mechuka](https://www.google.com/maps/@28.6320523,94.0662987,3a,49y,194.26h,92.18t,359.98r/data=!3m6!1e1!3m4!1smCvraPHUR1hld15MPCcP1Q!2e0!7i13312!8i6656?entry=ttu) the coverage gradually becomes overcast and somewhat dark.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: One far north-east valley (Mechuka) is the only place in the north-east with snowy mountains, with brownish grass and many Bhutan white pines. North of it the coverage turns overcast and dark.

differs.how: Bhutan white pine also grows near Bhutan border

text: The landscape south of Shillong in Meghalaya, is characterised by V-shaped, green eroded valleys with somewhat flat and smooth ridgetops.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: South of Shillong, green eroded V-shaped valleys with fairly flat, smooth ridge tops. Mizoram hills are less smooth, with more ups and downs.

clues.title: Landscape: salt flats and coastal marsh, almost no plants
text: Salt flats and [coastal marshes](https://www.google.com/maps/@22.0778782,72.2542147,3a,41.2y,236.56h,85.47t/data=!3m6!1e1!3m4!1sLYwEbQt8jOozBK8IYBl7ww!2e0!7i13312!8i6656?entry=ttu) with nearly **no vegetation**, other than short yellow or brown grass, can be found in parts of Gujarat. [Shallow bodies of water](https://goo.gl/maps/B8yUWPvxANcLtfMC8) can often be seen around these areas.
NOTE: The soil in western Rajasthan will be a lot more sandy and you’ll typically be able to see short desert shrubs.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: In parts of Gujarat, salt flats and coastal marshes with almost no plants but short yellow or brown grass, and shallow water. West Rajasthan has sandier soil and desert shrubs.

clues.title: Landscape: huge monolithic rock mountains
text: Near the southern tip of Tamil Nadu, you can find these large **monolithic mountains**, with huge exposed rocks. Several of these mountains can be seen from afar, especially the [Magenthiragiri hills](https://maps.app.goo.gl/qfZtnxhcLqxAxbzq9).

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Near the far southern tip, large monolithic mountains with huge exposed rock, visible from afar, especially the Mahendragiri hills.

clues.title: Landscape: flat bushy land with very red soil
text: A flat, bushy landscape with **very red soil** can be found in southern Tamil Nadu.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: South of Tamil Nadu has flat, bushy land with very red soil.

clues.title: Plants: coconut trees painted red and white

clues.summary: Lakshadweep, off the coast of Kerala, has abundant coconut trees, often painted red and white like the Polish flag.

clues.summary: Coverage on NH326 west of Brahmapur has a thin grey antenna and unusually high quality for this camera, especially near a reservoir.

clues.summary: Parts of NH6 and NH206 southeast of Shillong have khasi pines, yellow outer lines and fresh dark asphalt. It is the only road in Meghalaya with yellow edge lines, but other states have them too.

clues.title: Wind farms: where they cluster
text: The places with the most wind farms are indeed Gujarat, Karnataka, Maharashtra and Tamil Nadu. This is pretty advanced knowledge, but region guessing states can be possible by learning where wind farms are:
Gujarat: Southwestern half
Karnataka: Davanagere to Hubballi
Tamil Nadu: Max South; Around Coimbatore
Maharashtra: Tristate to Madhya and Gujarat; Around Jath (southern)
Rajasthan: Jodhpur to Jaisalmer
Madhya Pradesh: West & North of Indore

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.summary: Wind farms are most common in four states (Gujarat, Karnataka, Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu). Rough areas: south-west half of Gujarat; central Karnataka; far south and around Coimbatore; Maharashtra near the Madhya and Gujarat borders; Rajasthan between Jodhpur and Jaisalmer; west and north of Indore.
